links.comparator_used: Same model architectures trained without bias-mitigation methods (baseline), plus preprocessing and postprocessing mitigation approaches
links.outcome: FairOdds-AUC (AUROC adjusted by equalized odds gaps for sex and race/ethnicity) on internal and external test sets
links.effect: IPW improved FairOdds-AUC from 0.562 (95% CI 0.540, 0.581) to 0.600 (0.575, 0.629) for the transformer and from 0.556 (0.534, 0.577) to 0.5922 (0.53, 0.61919) for a fully connected network; adversarial fairness classifier reached up to 0.613 (0.595, 0.629) for the fully connected network; preprocessing/postprocessing FairOdds-AUC changes ranged from -0.009 to +0.021
links.tradeoff: Discrimination was essentially unchanged with IPW; postprocessing and preprocessing methods gave more variable changes and weaker generalizability across external sites
links.quote: Inprocessing methods, particularly inverse propensity weighting (IPW) and the adversarial fairness classifier, achieved more favorable fairness-performance tradeoffs than baseline and other mitigation approaches across all evaluation sets.

design_hint: bias mitigation (fairness-aware training/processing) with external site validation
